wu: Future Tense Charades: Write will, going to, might on cards. Students mime actions (e.g., 'I will travel to Paris') while others guess the form and meaning.
wuAlt: Plan Prediction Relay: Teams race to write sentences about future plans using correct forms (e.g., 'We are going to eat turkey').
Gratitude Brainstorm: Students share 3 things they 'will', 'are going to', or 'might do' to show gratitude this week.
pres: Show a picture of a Thanksgiving dinner. Model: 'I will cook the turkey (decision), I am going to invite my family (plan), I might try pumpkin pie (possibility).'. Use flashcards with icons (lightbulb for will, calendar for going to, question mark for might). Check understanding with thumbs up/down: 'Is this a plan or a prediction?'
presAlt: Real-life Stories: Teacher shares personal Thanksgiving plans, highlighting forms. Students repeat sentences.
Form Sorting Game: Display sentences on board; students group them into will/going to/might columns.
prac: Decision Roleplay: Pairs receive scenarios (e.g., 'Plan a Thanksgiving meal with $50 budget'). They negotiate using 'I will...', 'I am going to...', 'I might...'. Teacher monitors and corrects errors.
pracAlt: Form Match-Up: Cards with prompts (e.g., 'It's cloudy') and responses (e.g., 'It might rain'). Students match pairs.
Might Maze: Worksheet with paths; students write sentences using 'might' to describe possible outcomes.
ls: Listen to a dialogue about Thanksgiving plans. Students label sentences as will (W), going to (G), or might (M). Play twice; check answers in pairs.
re: Stand Up Sit Down: Teacher says sentences (e.g., 'I will eat turkey'). Students stand if it's a decision, sit if it's a plan, jump if it's a possibility.
prod: Gratitude Panel: Small groups discuss 'What will you do to show gratitude this year?'. Each member shares 1 plan (going to), 1 decision (will), and 1 possibility (might). Present to class.
rw: Read a short text about Thanksgiving traditions. Underline all future forms (will/going to/might). Then write 3 sentences about your own future plans using these forms.
st: Read a story about gratitude in different cultures (e.g., Moroccan 'Aïd' vs. Thanksgiving). End with: 'Today we practiced future forms for decisions, plans, and possibilities. Thank you for your participation!'
g: Students act out prompts (e.g., 'win the lottery') while others guess the form (will/going to/might).
Listen to a dialogue; draw arrows to show how plans change (e.g., 'We are going to... but we might...').
Ask 3 classmates: 'What will you do for gratitude?' and note responses.
Navigate a worksheet maze by writing 'might' sentences to describe possible paths.
Roleplay hosting a dinner; negotiate plans using all three future forms.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 50-word email inviting someone to Thanksgiving, using all three forms.
Support: Use a sentence frame: 'I will _____. I am going to _____. I might ____.'
hw: Write a thank-you email (80-100 words) to someone, using will/going to/might for future promises or plans.
Create a gratitude list with 5 items, using 'I will...' for actions and 'I might...' for hopes.
Record a 1-minute video explaining your Thanksgiving plans, using correct future forms.
tip: Link future forms to local contexts: e.g., 'I might visit my family during the Green March' or 'I will prepare for Eid by...'. This makes grammar relevant to learners' lives.
